chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Muḥammad ibn al-Nuʿmān, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: I perform istinjāʾ, then my garment falls into it while I am in janābah. So he said: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.أَسْتَنْجِي: I perform istinjāʾ, meaning I cleanse myself after relieving myself
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: a person in a state of janābah requiring ghusl
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is not considered problematic

ai.seo_question: Does a garment become problematic if it falls into the place of istinjāʾ while a person is junub?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purity and impurity. It indicates that in the case described, the falling of one's garment into the place of istinjāʾ while one is in janābah does not make it objectionable or problematic.
